reading.body:
CyrusOne Houston is the largest published data center campus in Texas by IT load capacity, holding 84 MW across two adjoined facilities, HOU3 and HOU4.

That 84 MW equals 18 percent of the 475 MW of IT capacity disclosed across 19 Texas facilities that publish power figures. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it translates to roughly 2,100 racks; at 10 kW per GPU, it could support about 8,400 high-end accelerators if fully allocated to GPU compute. The campus spans 347,000 square feet of technical space and holds a Green Globes certification, which signals energy efficiency operations but not AI workload specificity.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, but the vast majority publish no power figures, so the state's full capacity is unknown. CyrusOne Houston ranks first among the 19 facilities with disclosed capacity, but its true share of AI-ready power in Texas cannot be determined from public data. The campus is large enough to matter to AI scaling at the state level, yet whether its grid connection supports sustained AI training loads is not published.
